transcript:
This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place.
No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from the NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston. Flights are suspended at the main airport in the capital of Saudi Arabia.
Officials in Riyadh say a missile attack inside a passenger terminal on Saturday killed at least 12 people and wounded hundreds of others, some critically.
NPR's Aya Bittrawi reports.
This is the deadliest attack on the capital of Riyadh since 2015, when Saudi Arabia led a coalition of countries into war in Yemen against the Iran-backed Houthis.
Prior to Saturday's attack, the Houthis had already hit Riyadh's airport twice this week, piercing through Saudi Arabia's air defenses.
The group is also targeting airports in the south and east. The Houthis have declared Saudi airspace and airports as theaters of operations, with the exception, they say, of airports for Mecca and Medina.
The attacks come as Saudi forces and their Yemeni government allies carry out hundreds of airstrikes and attacks on the Houthis to try and recapture Yemeni territory along the Red Sea.
Aya Bittrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
Authorities have locked down large parts of New Delhi to block a youth-led protest. Demonstrators are demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner over changes to voter lists. The government denies wrongdoing.
President Trump rallied supporters in Tennessee last night ahead of next month's midterm elections. Mariana Bakayow of member station WPLN reports Trump says he came to celebrate Republican strength in the state.
Trump acknowledged that it's rare for him to stump for candidates in a ruby red state.
But I said, you know, sometimes it's nice to go to a place where you don't have to be, but you're there to say thank you to the great people that elected you three separate times in record month.
Trump touted the war in Iran and his decision to deploy the National Guard to Memphis as he addressed the crowd in Clarksville, Tennessee. Thousands braved the rain to see his rally, including Laurie Hoskins.
I just didn't know it's going to be close again, so I always got to say Trump. Hoskins is one of many voters in the state that will be voting in a new congressional district this November after the state re-districted at Trump's behest.
For NPR News, I'm Mariana Bakayow in Nashville.
Demonstrations are continuing in New York City over a shooting involving ICE agents. A 28-year-old Dominican national was shot on Thursday while driving in the Bronx with his five-year-old son in the back seat.
Protestor Iliana Lando says agents put the child in danger. I think it's completely inappropriate that he was shot at in his car with his five-year-old child. I am a teacher. I believe that we should protect all children no matter if their parents are criminals or not.
Just because you are a criminal does not mean that you deserve to die in front of your child.
The man's son was not injured. This is NPR.
Hurricane Simon has strengthened into a category four storm as it approaches Mexico's Pacific coast. Businesses and Puerto Vallarta have boarded up and authorities are evacuating coastal communities.
Forecasters say the storm could reach the coast today, bringing destructive waves and a dangerous storm surge.
In the southeast, cleanup operations continue after Hurricane Isaias made landfall in Florida on Friday. The storm has left at least four people dead and hundreds of thousands without electricity.
President Trump signed an executive order last week designed to help lower diesel costs for farmers, at least temporarily. South Dakota Public Broadcasting's Jackson Dirks reports.
Larry Bergen is loading soybeans into a truck. Trump's order lets farmers use dyed diesel in trucks like this until the end of the year.
It's exempt from federal taxes and normally reserved for off-road machinery. Bergen says it helps during harvest season.
We've got a long ways to go as far as how many times I'm going to fill. So it makes a lot of difference, yes.
It saves farmers about 24 cents a gallon in taxes, but diesel is still about 60 percent more expensive than this time last year. Scott Vanderwall is president of South Dakota's Farm Bureau.
It's a little bit of a band-aid. It certainly doesn't make up the difference.
Farmers helped Trump get into office. More than 60 percent of the vote in agriculture-heavy South Dakota went to Trump the last three elections.
For NPR News, I'm Jackson Dirks in Beersford, South Dakota. This is NPR News.
